title: Secure and Functional Code Generation with Self-Evaluation
title_zh: 基于自评估的安全且功能正确的代码生成

paragraphs.en: Large Language Models (LLMs) can generate functionally correct code that remains insecure. Security-focused fine-tuning can be expensive and is not always available, motivating inference-time approaches. Security-oriented prompting and retrieval can reduce vulnerabilities, but may also remove required behavior or apply defenses incompatible with the task. The challenge is to identify relevant security knowledge and use it to improve security without sacrificing functionality. We present SecGent , an inference-time framework that retrieves weakness context from the Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) database and applies it to secure code generation. By connecting task specifications to relevant textual CWE records, SecGent provides task-specific security guidance without relying on retrieved vulnerable or patched code examples. Complementary functional and security tests check the resulting implementation, and their execution feedback guides repairs toward satisfying both objectives. We evaluate SecGent with four open-source LLMs and Claude Sonnet 5.5 across five programming languages on the CWEval benchmark. It achieves the highest joint functional–security success against four inference-time baselines for all five models. Across the open-weight models, mean functional-security@1 (FS@1) improves by 15.5% over RAG, with gains in both functionality and security, and by 19.8% over the strongest prompt optimizer compiled for each model. On Sonnet, FS@1 reaches 92.1%, outperforming the strongest baseline AutoGen by 4.8%. In a separate comparison, SecGent outperforms Claude Code with security-focused prompting by over 6% in FS@1. Feedback-guided repair further improves FS@1 by up to 6.7% over generation without feedback, primarily by recovering functionality while checking security.

paragraphs.en: Large Language Models (LLMs) can generate code that performs its intended task but remains vulnerable to attack. LLM-based coding tools are increasingly becoming common ( Stack Overflow, 2025 ) , including GitHub Copilot ( GitHub, 2026 ) and assistants based on models such as GPT ( Achiam et al., 2023 ) , Claude ( Anthropic, 2024 ) , and Gemini ( Comanici et al., 2025 ) . This gap between functional correctness and security is consequential because passing ordinary tests does not establish that a program is secure (e.g., when handling adversarial inputs) ( Pearce et al., 2025 ; Siddiq and Santos, 2022 ; Bhatt et al., 2023 ; Peng et al., 2025 ) . Security-oriented interventions seek to close this gap, but can introduce another problem by rejecting valid inputs, removing required operations, or applying defenses incompatible with the task ( Dai et al., 2025 ) . LLM-based secure code generation must therefore address relevant weaknesses without losing the behavior developers require.
paragraphs.zh: 大语言模型（LLM）生成的代码可以完成其预期任务，但仍容易受到攻击。 基于 LLM 的编码工具正日益普及（Stack Overflow, 2025），包括 GitHub Copilot（GitHub, 2026）以及基于 GPT（Achiam et al., 2023）、Claude（Anthropic, 2024）和 Gemini（Comanici et al., 2025）等模型的智能体助手。 功能正确性与安全性之间的这一差距影响重大，因为通过普通测试并不能证明程序是安全的（例如在处理对抗性输入时）（Pearce et al., 2025；Siddiq and Santos, 2022；Bhatt et al., 2023；Peng et al., 2025）。 面向安全性的干预措施试图弥合这一差距，但可能会引入另一个问题：拒绝有效输入、移除必要的操作，或应用与任务不兼容的防御措施（Dai et al., 2025）。 因此，基于 LLM 的安全代码生成必须在解决相关弱点的同时，不丢失开发人员所需要的行为。

paragraphs.en: Consider a coding task from CWEval, a benchmark that evaluates both functional correctness and security using executable tests ( Peng et al., 2025 ) . The task asks for a JavaScript function that stores user-provided values in an HTTP response header. Figure 1 shows Qwen3-Coder-30B (Qwen30B)’s implementations. With Direct Prompting, the model stores the value without checking for carriage returns or newlines. The candidate passes the functional oracle, but an attacker-controlled value can inject additional header lines through a CWE-113 response-splitting weakness. All five sampled generations for this task exhibit the same failure. More broadly, 29.2% of functionally correct samples generated with Direct Prompting across our four open-weight models fail CWEval’s security oracle. Functional success alone therefore leaves substantial security risk unobserved. Prior works improve security through model adaptation, decoding constraints, and optimized prompts ( He and Vechev, 2023 ; He et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2024 ; Fu et al., 2024 ; Opsahl-Ong et al., 2024 ; Agrawal et al., 2026 ) . CodeGuarder ( Lin et al., 2025 ) and RESCUE ( Shi and Zhang, 2026 ) retrieve security explanations and code examples to guide generation. In our evaluation across the four open-weight models, providing task-relevant security context, such as CWE records, through Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) ( Lewis et al., 2020 ) improves mean security success over direct prompting but reduces functional correctness. This trade-off also appears in CodeGuarder, which retrieves vulnerability explanations and examples of vulnerable and patched code to guide generation. Its functional losses largely offset its security gains in joint functional–security success (Section 5.1 ). Figure 1 shows this trade-off. RAG checks for the injection characters, but also restricts Accept-Language to a single language tag. This rejects valid lists such as en-US,en;q=0.9 , so the candidate passes the security oracle but fails the functional oracle; four out of RAG’s five samples fail in this way. Improving security in isolation is therefore insufficient.

paragraphs.en: We introduce SecGent , an inference-time framework that retrieves weakness context : the CWE records most relevant to a given task, each describing in code-level terms the input, operation, and consequence that characterize the weakness. Its CWE-derived catalogue is constructed without using any specific benchmark task specifications or solutions. At inference time, Hypothetical Document Embedding (HyDE) query generation ( Gao et al., 2023 ) expresses plausible weaknesses of the requested operation, and reranking selects the five most relevant records. The coding agent receives this textual weakness context alongside the specification and is instructed to address the security risks while preserving required behavior. Our approach does not provide any vulnerable code or its corresponding patch examples to the coding agent. The same context guides complementary security and functional tests. For example, a security test checks that adversarial input does not trigger an unsafe effect, while a functional test checks that valid input produces the expected output. The testing agent selects a relevant weakness from the retrieved weakness context and turns its attacker-controlled input and observable effect into a security test, while a functional test checks specified behavior. Execution failures guide a bounded repair loop that permits at most a fixed number of repair attempts and retains a proposal only when it improves one generated-test objective without reducing the other. Prior work establishes the usefulness of execution feedback ( Chen et al., 2024 ; Nunez et al., 2024 ; Liang et al., 2026 ; Wang et al., 2026 ) ; SecGent focuses on retrieving weakness context for generation and candidate-independent frozen tests, with repair governed by an explicit two-objective retention rule.

paragraphs.en: Security of LLM-Generated Code. Prior studies consistently show that LLM-generated code can contain security weaknesses despite appearing functionally plausible ( Pearce et al., 2025 ; Tihanyi et al., 2023 ; Tihanyi et al., 2025 ; Hajipour et al., 2024 ) . Studies of LLM-native IDEs also report security and privacy risks in the surrounding development environment ( Akhond et al., 2026 ) . SecurityEval provides vulnerability-oriented programming tasks ( Siddiq and Santos, 2022 ) , and CyberSecEval evaluates security-sensitive generation prompts ( Bhatt et al., 2023 ) . SecVulEval ( Ahmed et al., 2026 ) benchmarks real-world C/C++ vulnerability detection using statement-level annotations and program context, and evaluates LLMs with a multi-agent pipeline. Its focus on detecting vulnerabilities in existing code complements our focus on secure generation and executable validation. CodeSecEval ( Wang et al., 2026 ) provides paired insecure and secure Python implementations with functional and vulnerability-targeted security tests for generation and repair. However, this benchmark is limited to Python language only. CWEval evaluates functionality and security on the same candidate using executable oracles ( Peng et al., 2025 ) . This joint assessment matters because a program can pass security checks by omitting required behavior; security-oriented interventions can therefore appear beneficial while reducing usefulness ( Dai et al., 2025 ) . We use joint functional–security success as the primary outcome and retain both constituent metrics to expose such trade-offs.
paragraphs.zh: LLM 生成代码的安全性。 已有研究一致表明，LLM 生成的代码尽管在功能上看似合理，却可能包含安全弱点（Pearce et al., 2025；Tihanyi et al., 2023；Tihanyi et al., 2025；Hajipour et al., 2024）。 针对 LLM 原生集成开发环境的研究也报告了其周边开发环境中的安全与隐私风险（Akhond et al., 2026）。 SecurityEval 提供面向漏洞的编程任务（Siddiq and Santos, 2022），CyberSecEval 则评估安全敏感的生成提示（Bhatt et al., 2023）。 SecVulEval（Ahmed et al., 2026）使用语句级标注和程序上下文对真实世界 C/C++ 漏洞检测进行基准测试，并通过多智能体流水线评估 LLM。 该基准侧重于检测现有代码中的漏洞，与我们侧重安全生成和可执行验证的工作形成互补。 CodeSecEval（Wang et al., 2026）提供了成对的不安全与安全 Python 实现，并附带功能性测试和面向漏洞的安全测试，用于生成与修复任务。 然而，该基准仅限于 Python 语言。 CWEval 使用可执行判定器在同一候选程序上同时评估功能性与安全性（Peng et al., 2025）。 这种联合评估十分重要，因为程序可以通过省略所需行为来通过安全检查；因此面向安全的干预措施可能在看似有益的同时降低了实用性（Dai et al., 2025）。 我们将功能与安全的联合成功作为主要结果指标，并保留两个构成指标以揭示此类权衡。

paragraphs.en: Secure Generation and Prompt Optimization. General code-generation research has developed open models such as CodeGen ( Nijkamp et al., 2022 ) and prompting approaches such as self-planning ( Jiang et al., 2024 ) and structured chain-of-thought ( Li et al., 2025 ) to improve implementation from natural-language specifications. SVEN ( He and Vechev, 2023 ) and SafeCoder ( He et al., 2024 ) adapt models for secure generation. Inference-time alternatives include constrained decoding ( Fu et al., 2024 ) , CoSec ( Li et al., 2024 ) , and security prompt optimization with PromSec ( Nazzal et al., 2024 ) . General prompt optimizers ( Khattab et al., 2023 ) such as MIPROv2 ( Opsahl-Ong et al., 2024 ) and GEPA ( Agrawal et al., 2026 ) , and selective prompt anchoring ( Tian and Zhang, 2025 ) , improve instructions, demonstrations, or their influence during generation. SecGent retrieves task-specific weakness context from a textual CWE catalogue to guide secure implementation, without model adaptation or benchmark-specific prompt compilation. Generated functional and security tests check the resulting behavior and guide repair.

paragraphs.en: Task-Aware Security Retrieval. CodeGuarder ( Lin et al., 2025 ) retrieves vulnerability explanations and examples of vulnerable and patched code from a ReposVul-derived knowledge base ( Wang et al., 2024 ) after decomposing the programming query into subtasks. RESCUE ( Shi and Zhang, 2026 ) combines distilled security guidelines with security-focused code examples and uses hierarchical, multi-faceted retrieval. Both select task-relevant knowledge to augment generation. SecGent shares this goal, but constructs weakness context from MITRE’s CWE records without retrieving code examples. Zero-shot catalogue rewriting and HyDE query generation connect task specifications to the vocabulary of software weaknesses, and reranking selects relevant records. The weakness context guides generation and the selection of a weakness for executable security testing. The testing agent grounds that weakness in task inputs and observable behavior without seeing the candidate.

paragraphs.en: Execution Feedback and Security Testing. Self-debugging and conversational generation use execution results to revise programs ( Chen et al., 2024 ; Han et al., 2025 ) , while vulnerability repair uses analysis feedback to guide patches ( Alrashedy et al., 2023 ) . AutoSafeCoder ( Nunez et al., 2024 ) combines a coding agent with LLM-based static analysis and mutation-based fuzzing that detects runtime crashes. SecTDD ( Liang et al., 2026 ) studies the effects of exposing security tests and returning execution failures, using supplied visible test partitions and independent hidden evaluation. These works establish that execution feedback is useful and coverage-dependent. SecAwareCoder ( Wang et al., 2026 ) derives CWE-linked vulnerability hypotheses and mitigation strategies from a stepwise solution blueprint to guide generation and testing. SecGent instead guides generation and testing with MITRE CWE records retrieved through catalogue rewriting, HyDE, and reranking. It validates and freezes tests before code generation, accepting repairs only if they improve functional or security test scores without lowering either. We could not include SecAwareCoder as a baseline because its replication package was unavailable at the time of writing.

paragraphs.en: SecGent uses retrieved CWE knowledge to guide generation and tests for required behavior and observable attack effects. Figure 2 shows a simplified example of the SecGent workflow. An offline step first builds a fixed weakness catalogue (Step 0); task-conditioned query generation, retrieval, and reranking select relevant records (Steps 1–3). A testing agent authors, validates, and freezes functional and security tests before any code exists (Step 4). A coding agent generates an implementation without seeing the tests (Step 5), which are then executed against it (Step 6). Failure diagnostics (Step 7) guide the same coding agent’s repair proposals (Step 8). A proposal replaces the retained candidate only if re-execution improves one tested objective without reducing the other (Step 9).

paragraphs.en: A MITRE record describes a weakness through its flaw and consequences, whereas a programming task describes the functionality to implement and seldom names a weakness. We therefore use the rewrite to name the input, the operation, and the consequence in the vocabulary a developer would use. For CWE-117, MITRE states that “the product constructs a log message from external input, but it does not neutralize …” . The rewritten description reads “user-supplied data is written directly to log …” , with keywords such as log , format , and write . The rewrite sees only source text. In Section 6.3 , we empirically show why such a catalogue is necessary for accurate retrieval. When MITRE publishes an updated release, the same extraction, rewriting, and embedding procedure can be rerun periodically to produce a new catalogue for subsequent inference. paragraphs.en: Weakness Context Retrieval. A coding task describes the behavior to implement, whereas CWE records describe patterns of insecure behavior. This vocabulary mismatch makes direct retrieval difficult. For example, the running task (Figure 2 ) asks the model to construct a log entry, but does not mention log injection, or record separators. To bridge this gap, SecGent adapts Hypothetical Document Embeddings (HyDE) ( Gao et al., 2023 ) . Rather than searching only with the task specification, the query writer h ϕ h_{\phi} generates a hypothetical vulnerable implementation of the task together with a brief explanation of the operation or missing check that could make it insecure. This hypothetical analysis need not be correct; its purpose is to express the task in the code- and weakness-oriented vocabulary used by the generated catalogue. The generated text is then combined with the original task specification to retrieve CWE records that are semantically close to plausible insecure realizations of the task. Retrieval then proceeds in two stages,

paragraphs.en: The test-execution layer bridges the language-independent invoke interface used by generated tests to the language-specific way a candidate must be built and called. An adapter materializes the candidate and benchmark entry point, performs any required compilation or loading, invokes the function, and normalizes its observable result. This lets the testing agent express the same kind of assertion for Python, C, C++, Go, and JavaScript without encoding build or process details in the generated test suite. Each code candidate is evaluated against the frozen test suite in a fresh, throwaway Docker-compatible container. Subprocess and outer timeouts bound execution. The harness separates build failures from assertion failures and classifies the result as candidate evidence (build diagnostics or named functional/security outcomes), a complete pass, or an unusable test suite. An unusable test suite—for example, one that cannot be imported or reported reliably—does not support a conclusion about candidate quality and cannot trigger repair.

paragraphs.en: Prompt Optimizers. We evaluate three methods that optimize the code-generation prompt on the training partition (Section 5.2 ). GEPA ( Agrawal et al., 2026 ) revises the instructions using textual feedback from executed evaluations, with the evaluated model acting as both reflector and generator. Each method outputs a reusable prompt, a compiled program , which is then applied unchanged to held-out tasks with their specifications and retrieved weakness context.

paragraphs.en: Large Language Models. The experiments cover two general-purpose LLMs, GPT-OSS-20B (GPT-OSS) and Gemma-4-26B (Gemma4), and two code language models, Qwen2.5-Coder-14B (Qwen14B) and Qwen3-Coder-30B (Qwen30B). To examine whether the findings hold for a frontier proprietary model, we additionally evaluate Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Sonnet-5.5) against the inference-time baselines and in the language-specific and paired repair analyses. The prompt optimizers are applied to the four open-weight models. RQ1 identifies RAG and AutoGen as the strongest baselines at FS@1 across models and establishes SecGent ’s consistent advantage over them across all five models. We therefore focus the proprietary evaluation on these common inference-time comparisons and limit RQ2 to the open-weight models because compiling each optimizer entails repeated generation and evaluation on the training tasks, adding substantial API cost for Sonnet. We use the short names throughout the remainder of the paper. Every reported method uses five independently sampled candidates per task and temperature 0.8 (excluding Sonnet-5.5, which does not allow temperature changes), and we report k ∈ { 1 , 2 , 5 } k\in\{1,2,5\} . SecGent permits at most two test-generation attempts and two repair proposals. We serve all open-weight models locally using Ollama and access Sonnet-5.5 through the Anthropic API.

paragraphs.en: Embedding Model. We encode the CWE records and every task query with Qwen3-Emb-8B ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) and retrieve by dense similarity over these embeddings. paragraphs.en: CWE Database. Retrieval draws on a fixed catalogue of 944 weaknesses from MITRE’s Research Concepts view (CWE-1000) ( MITRE, 2026 ) , which organises weaknesses by abstract behaviour rather than by language or domain and thus gives the broadest coverage of software weaknesses. We build the catalogue in two steps. First, we take each weakness’s identifier, name, description, and potential mitigations from the MITRE records. Second, an LLM (Qwen3.8:27b) is prompted once, in a zero-shot setting, with the MITRE name and description of each weakness and rewrites them into a one-sentence description and a short list of code-level keywords, that name the input, operation, and consequence in the vocabulary a developer would use. The generation does not involve any benchmark task. Each entry thus holds the identifier, name, generated description, keywords, and MITRE mitigations. The catalogue is built offline and frozen before the experiments.

paragraphs.en: Retrieval Pipeline. Given the task’s language and specification, the query writer identifies an operation that could make the code vulnerable. It describes how that operation could be implemented insecurely and explains the resulting weakness without naming a CWE. We combine these last two descriptions with the task specification to form the retrieval query. Each CWE record is embedded using its name, rewritten description, keywords, and up to 600 characters of MITRE mitigations. We retrieve the 20 records whose embeddings are most similar to the query embedding.
paragraphs.zh: 检索流水线。 给定任务的语言和规范，查询编写器识别出一种可能使代码存在漏洞的操作。 它描述该操作可能如何被不安全地实现，并解释由此导致的弱点，但不指名具体的 CWE。 我们将后两种描述与任务规范结合起来，构成检索查询。 每条 CWE 记录使用其名称、改写后的描述、关键词以及最多 600 个字符的 MITRE 缓解措施进行嵌入。 我们检索出与查询嵌入最相似的 20 条记录。

paragraphs.en: The reranker compares each record’s name and description with the operation and insecure implementation described by the query writer, assigning a relevance score from 0 to 100. It scores all 20 records together in three calls: one in retrieval order and two in shuffled orders. We average the scores to reduce the influence of candidate order, then use the five highest-scoring records to guide code and test generation. We use qwen3.8:27b for query writing and reranking and reuse each task’s retrieved records across all evaluated models.

paragraphs.en: Results. Table 1 shows that SecGent achieves the highest joint functional–security success for every model at k = 1 k{=}1 and 5 5 . paragraphs.en: Security–Functionality Trade-offs. The baselines expose a recurring failure mode of security-oriented prompting. On the open-weight models, RAG raises mean S@1 by 30.0% over Direct Prompting, but does so while reducing functional correctness. The trade-off is sharper for CodeGuarder: its mean F@1 falls by 17.6% compared with Direct Prompting, and the resulting mean FS@1 is effectively unchanged. Security gains alone therefore need not translate into joint success: FS@1 requires the same candidate to satisfy both the functional and security oracles. AutoGen shows the opposite profile. Its reviewer improves functional correctness, giving the highest mean F@1 among the baselines (79.1%, 8.4% above Direct Prompting), but its mean S@1 of 62.4% remains 11.4% below RAG, which limits its mean FS@1 to 59.1%. General-purpose review thus recovers functionality but leaves more security failures. On Sonnet-5.5, RAG avoids this trade-off and improves both F@1 and S@1 over Direct Prompting, whereas CodeGuarder again lowers F@1, by 14.1%, and its FS@1 falls 14.3% below Direct Prompting.
paragraphs.zh: 安全性–功能性权衡。 这些基线方法暴露了面向安全的提示词的一种常见失败模式。 在开放权重模型上，RAG 使平均 S@1 相比 Direct Prompting 提升了 30.0%，但其代价是降低了功能正确性。 CodeGuarder 的权衡更为明显：其平均 F@1 相比 Direct Prompting 下降了 17.6%，而最终的平均 FS@1 几乎没有变化。 因此，仅靠安全性的提升并不一定带来联合成功：FS@1 要求同一个候选解同时通过功能性测试与安全性测试。 AutoGen 则呈现出相反的表现。 其审查环节提升了功能正确性，取得了各基线方法中最高的平均 F@1（79.1%，比 Direct Prompting 高 8.4%），但其 62.4% 的平均 S@1 仍比 RAG 低 11.4%，这使其平均 FS@1 仅停留在 59.1%。 因此，通用型的代码审查虽然恢复了功能性，却留下了更多安全失败。 在 Sonnet-5.5 上，RAG 避免了这一权衡，相比 Direct Prompting 同时提升了 F@1 和 S@1；而 CodeGuarder 再次降低了 F@1，降幅为 14.1%，其 FS@1 则比 Direct Prompting 低 14.3%。

paragraphs.en: Approach. Prompt optimizers learn from benchmark examples, hence, they must be evaluated on unseen tasks. We split CWEval by task family, where a family is one CWE scenario across languages. We divide CWEval into 71 training tasks from 23 families and 48 held-out tasks from 13 families (60–40 split). BootstrapFewShot, MIPROv2, and GEPA (Section 4.3 ) are compiled on the training tasks for each of the four open-weight models, and every method is evaluated on the held-out tasks with five samples per task. We restrict prompt optimization to the four open-weight models as compiling the optimizers for Sonnet-5.5 would incur substantial API costs.
paragraphs.zh: 方法。 提示词优化器从基准测试样本中学习，因此必须在未见过的任务上进行评估。 我们按任务族对 CWEval 进行划分，一个任务族是指同一种 CWE 场景在不同语言下的任务集合。 我们将 CWEval 划分为来自 23 个任务族的 71 个训练任务和来自 13 个任务族的 48 个留出任务（60–40 划分）。 BootstrapFewShot、MIPROv2 和 GEPA（第 4.3 节）在四个开源权重模型各自的训练任务上进行编译，每种方法都在留出任务上进行评估，每个任务使用五个样本。 我们将提示词优化限制在四个开源权重模型上，因为为 Sonnet-5.5 编译优化器会产生高昂的 API 成本。

paragraphs.en: Results. As Figure 5 shows, SecGent achieves the highest overall FS@1 for every model, with overall gains of 10.8–15.8% over the best overall baseline on the open-weight models and 7.2% on Sonnet-5.5. Averaging each method’s language-specific FS@1 equally across the open-weight models, it also ranks first in every language. This consistency extends to individual model–language combinations: SecGent ranks first or second in 19 of the 20 open-weight comparisons (5 languages × \times 4 models), outperforms RAG in all 20, CodeGuarder in 19, and AutoGen in 17. On Sonnet-5.5, it ranks first in C, C++, and Python and second to RAG in Go. The gain therefore extends to both retrieval-based baselines, despite their different forms of security knowledge, and is not confined to languages where prompt optimization performs poorly.

paragraphs.en: Language Sensitivity of Prompt Optimizers. Prompt optimization can improve joint success in one language while weakening it in another. On Qwen30B, GEPA improves Python performance but reduces Go FS@1 by 79.4% compared with Direct Prompting. MIPROv2 shows a milder version of the same pattern on Gemma4, improving JavaScript performance but reducing joint success in Go. SecGent remains competitive or better in the languages where these optimizers improve, while achieving much stronger Go results than either optimizer. This variation matters when a single compiled prompt is reused for tasks in several languages.
paragraphs.zh: 提示词优化器的语言敏感性。 提示词优化可以在一种语言中提升联合成功率，却在另一种语言中削弱它。 在 Qwen30B 上，与 Direct Prompting 相比，GEPA 提升了 Python 性能，但使 Go 的 FS@1 降低了 79.4%。 MIPROv2 在 Gemma4 上表现出同一模式的较温和版本，提升了 JavaScript 性能，但降低了 Go 中的联合成功率。 在这些优化器有所提升的语言中，SecGent 保持竞争力或更优，同时在 Go 上取得远强于两个优化器的结果。 当同一个编译后的提示词被复用于多种语言的任务时，这种差异尤为重要。

paragraphs.en: GEPA’s decline on Go includes functional failures on tasks that Direct Prompting can already solve. SecGent preserves Direct Prompting’s functional accuracy and achieves much stronger security than GEPA on these tasks. These differences may arise from reusing a single optimized prompt across languages. Although optimization uses a multilingual training set, the selected prompt can emphasize only a few languages. For example, BootstrapFewShot’s optimized prompts contain only C demonstrations in all four models. These are LLM-generated examples selected for their functional and security success. The model therefore receives worked examples of secure C code even when asked to generate code in another language. Instruction optimization can also show the same imbalance, such as, GEPA’s prompt for Qwen30B gives concrete API advice for Python and detailed implementation rules for C and JavaScript, but no Go-specific guidance. Such advice may help in the languages it addresses yet transfer poorly when another language requires different APIs or error handling. These patterns suggest that language-specific solutions learned during optimization may limit gains in other languages. SecGent applies security guidance to the current task and checks the resulting code with task-specific tests, helping preserve functionality across languages.
paragraphs.zh: GEPA 在 Go 语言上的性能下降包括了一些 Direct Prompting 已经能够解决的任务上的功能性失败。 SecGent 保持了 Direct Prompting 的功能准确性，并在这些任务上实现了远强于 GEPA 的安全性。 这些差异可能源于在多种语言间复用同一个优化后的提示词。 尽管优化使用的是多语言训练集，所选出的提示词可能只侧重少数几种语言。 例如，BootstrapFewShot 优化后的提示词在全部四个模型中都只包含 C 语言的示例。 这些是由大语言模型生成的、因功能和安全性方面表现出色而被选中的示例。 因此，即使要求模型用另一种语言生成代码，它也会接收到安全的 C 代码的示范示例。 指令优化也可能表现出同样的失衡，例如，GEPA 针对 Qwen30B 的提示词为 Python 提供了具体的 API 建议，为 C 和 JavaScript 提供了详细的实现规则，却没有针对 Go 的指导。 这类建议在其所涉及的语言中可能有帮助，但当另一种语言需要不同的 API 或错误处理方式时，迁移效果可能不佳。 这些模式表明，优化过程中学到的针对特定语言的解决方案可能会限制在其他语言中的收益。 SecGent 将安全指导应用于当前任务，并使用任务特定的测试检查生成的代码，从而有助于在跨语言场景下保持功能性。

paragraphs.en: Magnitude of Per-Language Differences. Each language in the test split contains only 8–13 tasks, hence, a shortfall of SecGent can reflect differences on very few tasks. For example, the 2.9% FS@1 shortfall against Direct Prompting on Qwen30B’s Go tasks comes from a lower success rate on just one of nine tasks; the methods tie on the other eight. Yet SecGent outperforms Direct Prompting in all four other languages on the same model. Similarly, the largest shortfall, 9.1% against MIPROv2 on Gemma4’s JavaScript tasks, comes from a lower success rate on one of eight tasks, partly offset by higher rates on two others. MIPROv2 also trails SecGent in all four other languages on Gemma4. On Sonnet-5.5, SecGent trails all four baselines in JavaScript because it succeeds on four rather than five samples of a single task; all methods tie on the remaining seven. These examples show that the local advantages belong to different baselines and concern small task sets, while SecGent maintains competitive performance across languages.

paragraphs.en: This pattern is consistent with the functional losses observed under security-oriented generation in RQ1 and RQ2. Of the 58 security improvements, 48 accompany functional recovery, including 30 candidates that initially fail to build and are therefore scored as both non-functional and insecure. paragraphs.en: Representative Example. Figure 6 illustrates this complementary role of the tests. CWEval labels the C++ redirect task CWE-020, while the testing agent selects CWE-187 (partial string comparison) from the weakness context. This weakness is still relevant because a partial domain match can cause the task’s input validation to accept an unauthorized redirect. The security test checks that example.com.attacker.com is rejected. This host belongs to attacker.com , even though its name contains the allowed domain example.com . paragraphs.en: Ablation: Task-Level Effectiveness of Test Feedback. We evaluate the task-level effectiveness of generated-test feedback by comparing SecGent with and without feedback-guided repair. Both configurations use the same retrieval, code-generation prompt, 119 tasks, and five samples per task. Table 4 reports this comparison for Gemma4, Qwen30B, and Sonnet-5.5. Across the four open-weight models, feedback improves mean FS@1 by 2.6%, with gains also at FS@2 and FS@5. Mean functionality and security both improve. FS@1 increases for all five models: Gemma4 gains the most at 6.7%, followed by Sonnet-5.5 at 3.0%, while the remaining models gain 0.6–1.8%.
paragraphs.zh: 消融实验：测试反馈在任务层面的有效性。 我们通过比较有无反馈引导修复的 SecGent，评估生成测试反馈在任务层面的有效性。 两种配置使用相同的检索、代码生成提示、119 个任务以及每个任务五个样本。 表 4 报告了 Gemma4、Qwen30B 和 Sonnet-5.5 的这一比较结果。 在四个开源权重模型上，反馈将平均 FS@1 提升了 2.6%，FS@2 和 FS@5 也有提升。 平均功能性和安全性均有提高。 所有五个模型的 FS@1 均有提升：Gemma4 提升最多，达 6.7%，其次是 Sonnet-5.5，为 3.0%，其余模型的提升为 0.6–1.8%。

paragraphs.en: General-purpose coding agents plan, write, and execute code, which raises the question of whether such a harness can implement code that is both functional and secure. We therefore run Claude Code ( Anthropic, 2025 ) with Sonnet-5.5 on the 48 held-out tasks, with five independent sessions per task. The agent receives a task specification under one of two prompts: a functionality-focused prompt, which asks the agent to verify that its code compiles and behaves as specified, and a security-focused prompt, which asks for code that is both functional and secure but without providing any CWE context.
paragraphs.zh: 通用编程智能体负责规划、编写并执行代码，这引出一个问题：这样的框架能否实现既功能正常又安全可靠的代码。 因此，我们在 48 个留出任务上运行 Claude Code（Anthropic，2025），使用 Sonnet-5.5，每个任务进行五次独立会话。 智能体在两种提示词之一下接收任务规范：一种是功能导向提示词，要求智能体验证其代码能够编译并按规范运行；另一种是安全导向提示词，要求代码既功能正常又安全，但不提供任何 CWE 相关背景信息。

paragraphs.en: Table 5 shows that the functionality-focused configuration attains the highest F@1 (94.2%), yet its S@1 is only 87.1% and its FS@5 saturates at 87.5% such that six tasks remain insecure in all five sessions. Checking that code behaves as specified does not expose the weaknesses it contains. The security-focused instruction raises S@1 to 91.2%, but F@1 falls to 88.8% resulting in a slight improvement of FS@1 to 87.9%. SecGent achieves the highest S@1 and FS@ k k at every k k , improving FS@1 by 6.2% relative to the stronger configuration while maintaining comparable functionality. This analysis shows that a capable agentic harness with execution access can still be prone to insecure code generation, and a generic security instruction exchanges functionality for security rather than achieving both supporting to our findings in RQ1 and RQ2.
paragraphs.zh: 表 5 显示，以功能为中心的配置取得了最高的 F@1（94.2%），但其 S@1 仅为 87.1%，且其 FS@5 饱和在 87.5%，导致六个任务在全部五次会话中始终不安全。 检查代码是否按规范运行，并不能暴露其内部存在的安全弱点。 以安全为中心的指令将 S@1 提升至 91.2%，但 F@1 降至 88.8%，使得 FS@1 仅略有提升至 87.9%。 SecGent 在每个 k 值上都取得了最高的 S@1 和 FS@k，相对于更强的配置将 FS@1 提升了 6.2%，同时保持了相当的功能性。 这一分析表明，具备执行权限的强大智能体框架仍可能生成不安全的代码，而通用的安全指令是以牺牲功能性来换取安全性，而非两者兼得，这支持了我们在 RQ1 和 RQ2 中的发现。

paragraphs.en: Failure Sources. The 11 joint regressions in RQ4 account for 3.8% of the 291 retained repairs, despite improvements in their generated-test scores. Among the ten open-weight regressions, three involve incorrect functional expectations, five involve security assertions that reward unsafe behavior, and two involve incomplete functional coverage. One security test, for example, expects ten bytes of content from a five-byte buffer. In the two CWE-113 cases, repairs reject all header values containing spaces, while a functional test using only en-US misses valid values such as gzip, deflate . The additional Sonnet regression occurs on a Go CWE-943 task following a build failure in the generated-test environment, a retained repair removes the SQLite driver import but then fails both CWEval objectives. This also highlights the need for compatibility between the repair and evaluation environments.

paragraphs.en: Effect on Repairs. Figure 7 shows how an incorrect expectation can actively drive a regression. A generated test requires the directory’s own name in the output of ls -l , although this command lists the directory’s contents. The repair fabricates an entry to satisfy this assertion, turning a candidate that passes both CWEval oracles into one that fails functionality. The Pareto gate retains it because both generated tests pass. Two other repairs are retained despite still failing one generated test. The Pareto gate accepts them because they pass a previously failing test without causing any previously passing test to fail. These cases motivate future work on adapting existing methods for test validation to improve the reliability of both functional and CWE-aware security tests generated before implementation.

paragraphs.en: Retrieval Coverage. Table 8 compares retrieval over all 119 tasks. Direct dense retrieval uses the task specification to search embeddings of MITRE’s original CWE-1000 records ( MITRE, 2026 ) , without rewriting their descriptions or generating a HyDE query. Recall counts the benchmark CWE or a direct child as a correct match. Direct retrieval achieves 47.1% recall among the top five records, increasing to 67.2% with reranking. With SecGent ’s rewritten catalogue (Section 3.2 ) and HyDE query (Section 3.3 ), recall reaches 75.6% before reranking and 89.1% afterward. These results support the combined catalogue and query design for bridging the vocabulary gap between task requirements and weakness descriptions.

paragraphs.en: Relevance Beyond the Benchmark Label. Missing the benchmark CWE does not always mean missing a relevant weakness. Among the 13 misses, four tasks retrieve a CWE relevant to their security tests. For example, the three cwe_327_2 tasks are labeled CWE-327 (unsafe cryptographic algorithms). Their tests also check for random initialization vectors (IVs, starting values used in encryption), making the retrieved CWE-329 (predictable IVs) relevant. Even on the 13 tasks where SecGent did not retrieve the weakness named by the benchmark, 64.6% of its generated programs passed the security tests, compared with 47.7% for Direct Prompting. This suggests that related weakness context may still provide useful security guidance.
paragraphs.zh: 超越基准标签之外的相关性。 未命中基准 CWE 并不总是意味着遗漏了相关的弱点。 在 13 个未命中的任务中，有四个任务检索到了与其安全测试相关的 CWE。 例如，三个 cwe_327_2 任务被标记为 CWE-327（不安全的加密算法）。 它们的测试还检查了随机初始化向量（IV，即加密中使用的起始值），这使得检索到的 CWE-329（可预测的 IV）具有相关性。 即使在 SecGent 未能检索到基准所指弱点的 13 个任务中，其生成的程序也有 64.6% 通过了安全测试，而直接提示（Direct Prompting）的这一比例为 47.7%。 这表明相关弱点的上下文仍然可以提供有用的安全指导。

paragraphs.en: Internal Validity. LLM generation and test execution are stochastic, which may affect individual outcomes. We mitigate this by sampling five candidates per task and holding the model identifier, decoding settings, sample count, and evaluation split fixed within each comparison. Generated test suites may also be incomplete or incorrect. To avoid treating them as ground truth, they are used only to guide repair; all reported functional and security outcomes are determined independently by CWEval. Unusable generated test suites trigger no repair, and the initial candidate is retained instead.
paragraphs.zh: 内部有效性。 大语言模型生成与测试执行具有随机性，可能会影响个别结果。 我们通过在每次比较中对每个任务采样五个候选，并保持模型标识符、解码设置、采样数量和评估划分固定不变来缓解这一问题。 生成的测试套件也可能不完整或存在错误。 为避免将其视为真值，这些测试套件仅用于指导修复；所有报告的功能性和安全性结果均由 CWEval 独立判定。 无法使用的生成测试套件不会触发修复，而是保留初始候选。

paragraphs.en: External Validity. We evaluate four open-weight LLMs and Claude Sonnet 5.5 on all 119 CWEval tasks for RQ1 and RQ4, and on 48 family-disjoint tasks for RQ3. RQ2 evaluates prompt optimizers only on the four open-weight models; their comparison on Sonnet remains outside the scope of this study. Including Sonnet extends the evidence to a proprietary API model, but does not establish generalization across proprietary model families. The benchmark spans five programming languages and 31 weakness classes. Although this provides diversity across models, languages, and weaknesses, CWEval consists of function-level programming tasks and may not represent repository-scale development, long-context interactions, or proprietary coding assistants. Generalization to such settings therefore requires further study.

paragraphs.en: We presented SecGent , an inference-time framework that connects programming tasks to relevant CWE knowledge for generation, testing, and repair. Our findings suggest that security guidance is most useful when grounded in the task’s required behavior and checked alongside functionality. Execution feedback primarily recovers functionality, while security test check whether repairs preserve the tested protections; the reliability of these repairs depends on the correctness and coverage of generated tests. Across five models and five languages, SecGent achieves the highest joint functional–security success among the evaluated inference-time baselines, including Claude Code. Future work should extend the catalogue with additional weakness and vulnerability databases, such as NVD through CWE mappings, and assess whether broader knowledge improves retrieval and security coverage. It should also validate generated security tests against vulnerable and corrected variants, broaden valid-input coverage, and evaluate the framework in repository-scale development.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 SecGent，这是一个推理时框架，将编程任务与相关的 CWE 知识相连接，用于生成、测试和修复。 我们的研究结果表明，安全指导只有在立足于任务所需的行为并与功能性一同检查时才最为有用。 执行反馈主要用于恢复功能性，而安全测试则检查修复是否保留了已测试的保护措施；这些修复的可靠性取决于所生成测试的正确性和覆盖率。 在五个模型和五种语言上，SecGent 在所评估的推理时基线（包括 Claude Code）中实现了最高的功能–安全联合成功率。 未来的工作应通过更多的弱点与漏洞数据库来扩展该目录，例如通过 CWE 映射接入 NVD，并评估更广泛的知识是否能提升检索和安全覆盖率。 还应针对易受攻击的变体和已修正的变体验证所生成的安全测试，扩大有效输入的覆盖范围，并在仓库规模的开发中评估该框架。

sents.en: We presented SecGent , an inference-time framework that connects programming tasks to relevant CWE knowledge for generation, testing, and repair.
sents.zh: 我们提出了 SecGent，这是一个推理时框架，将编程任务与相关的 CWE 知识相连接，用于生成、测试和修复。

sents.en: Our findings suggest that security guidance is most useful when grounded in the task’s required behavior and checked alongside functionality.
sents.zh: 我们的研究结果表明，安全指导只有在立足于任务所需的行为并与功能性一同检查时才最为有用。

sents.en: Execution feedback primarily recovers functionality, while security test check whether repairs preserve the tested protections; the reliability of these repairs depends on the correctness and coverage of generated tests.

sents.en: Across five models and five languages, SecGent achieves the highest joint functional–security success among the evaluated inference-time baselines, including Claude Code.
sents.zh: 在五个模型和五种语言上，SecGent 在所评估的推理时基线（包括 Claude Code）中实现了最高的功能–安全联合成功率。

sents.en: It should also validate generated security tests against vulnerable and corrected variants, broaden valid-input coverage, and evaluate the framework in repository-scale development.
